title: Kernel contracts and onboarding playbook for mixture architectures
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary:
This ticket defines a repeatable onboarding playbook and a lightweight kernel 'contract' manifest model for models with mixed attention/expert patterns (standard MHA, grouped-query attention (GQA), and Mixture-of-Experts (MoE)). The objective is to produce machine-readable kernel capability manifests + a human-guided checklist that allow the compilation pipeline and runtime router to safely pin kernel builds per model variant while preserving rollback and graceful fallback policies.

Why this is needed:
- We repeatedly see per-model performance variance across attention variants and expert sharding. Blindly picking the top-performing kernel sometimes regresses tail latency for long sequences or edge hardware.
- Customers pin model versions for SLAs; we need a first-class way to publish per-model kernel profile recommendations and enforce safe rollout.

Goals / Acceptance criteria:
1) Kernel contract schema (JSON/YAML) that includes: supported op patterns (MHA/GQA/MoE), expected sequence-length buckets, preferred data types (fp16/int8/q4 variants), required kernel flags (e.g. continuous-batching-enabled), KV cache compatibility, and fallback order with estimated latency/cost bands.
2) Onboarding checklist and automated validation: a) deterministic perf sweep across sequence-length buckets and batch sizes; b) correctness regression tests (sampling, logits compare, end-to-end chat sims); c) resource/oom safety checks for sharded MoE.
3) Publish workflow: a model onboarding PR that publishes kernel manifest to model-catalog, attaches perf dashboards (Grafana link), and tags recommended pin in the model registry.
4) Runtime: ability to read pinned manifests, enforce pin at request-routing time, and automatically fall back to safe default profile if runtime capability mismatch occurs.
5) Rollout plan: canary (1% traffic) -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with automatic rollback on latency/cost regressions defined by thresholds in manifest.
6) Telemetry: token-level latency distribution, p95/p99, memory headroom, KV cache hit rates, model-quality regression metrics for canonical eval prompts.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Strong pinning increases stability but reduces ability for live kernel upgrades. To balance this we require an explicit pin TTL and encourage version aliases (e.g. stable, experimental). Pins will be enforced only for customers who opt into pinned deployments (Dedicated/Private plus opt-in hosted tiers).
- For MoE, we specify a minimum safe headroom for expert routing memory; if headroom not available, runtime must route to a compatible non-MoE fallback profile. This avoids OOMs at scale but may increase cost for heavy traffic.
- Quantized kernels (q4/q8) are allowed in manifests but must include bit-exactness tolerance buckets in correctness tests and a quality-monitoring overlay in the console.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Schema proposal and RFC (this ticket) with example manifests for a small GPT-MHA, a GQA variant, and a sharded MoE prototype.
2) Perf harness updates: parameterized sweeps by seq_len/batch and an automated exporter that writes structured perf artifacts to the onboarding PR.
3) Model-catalog API: support manifest ingestion and pin metadata (pin author, TTL, rationale, canary configuration).
4) Runtime changes: manifest reader, pin enforcement on the router, and fallback resolution algorithm.
5) Console: surface pinned profile, canary state, and regression alerts tied to the manifest thresholds.
6) Docs & playbook: a step-by-step guide for external model teams and SREs.

Acceptance test examples:
- GPT-style MHA profile: p50 latency under 40ms for seq_len 128 @ batch 8 on a4x; must pass logits-diff < 1e-4 on canonical prompt set.
- GQA profile: stability across seq_len 512 with KV cache enabled; must not regress p99 by >10% compared to baseline.
- MoE profile: expert sharding should remain within memory headroom threshold across 95th percentile request size; fallback to quantized non-MoE when headroom < threshold.

Links and artifacts:
- PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/x/Onb-Playbook (internal)
- Perf dashboard (canary): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/hybrid-kernel-onboard/summary
- Example manifests: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/kernel-manifests-2026
- Draft RFC (diff): https://github.com/redwood-ai/runtime/pull/2348
- Onboarding test harness: https://github.com/redwood-ai/perf-harness/tree/feature/kernel-contracts

Open questions / blockers:
- Driver-level differences for new quant kernels on partner cloud GPUs (we need a compatibility matrix from infra).
- Which teams own the pin TTL and who has the authority to bump a pin? Proposal: model-owner (onboarder) creates pin; infra or runtime SRE can revoke for emergency rollback.
- Integration with Dedicated autopilot: how do we expose pin enforcement to customers who run Reserved capacity? Need product alignment with Dedicated PM.

Next steps:
- Collect feedback from compiler and serving leads in design review (scheduled 2026-03-12).
- Prototype schema validation in perf-harness and post example manifests into model-catalog staging.
- Short spike to measure MoE headroom detection in staging.
